q: 1. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: An excess of coarser particles relative to fines reduces the paste's ability to lubricate the mix, making the concrete harsh and difficult to work.

q: 2. Ferro-concrete is another name given to (Ferror = iron)
explain: Ferro-concrete literally means iron-concrete, referring to concrete reinforced with steel (iron) bars, i.e., reinforced cement concrete.

q: 3. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is
explain: Iron oxide is present in the smallest percentage (about 3-4%) among the major ingredients (lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide) of cement.

q: 4. The cement concrete in which high compressive stressed are artificially induced before its actual use, is called
explain: Prestressed concrete has internal compressive stresses artificially induced (via tensioned tendons) before loading, so that tensile stresses from service loads are offset.

q: 5. The cement whose strength is little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement develops strength slowly at early stages due to lower C3S and C3A content, but eventually catches up with the strength of ordinary cement after about three months.

q: 6. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is interground with clinker specifically to control/retard the otherwise flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 7. The gypsum is added to the cement for
options: providing high strength to the cement
controlling the initial setting time of cement
lowering the initial setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard/control the initial setting time of cement, preventing flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 8. The diameter of needle in vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: For the initial setting time test, the Vicat needle used has a cross-sectional diameter of 1 mm as per IS specifications.

q: 9. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinkers is about
explain: Portland pozzolana cement is manufactured by blending about 30% pozzolanic material with ordinary Portland cement clinker.

q: 10. For ordinary portland cement
options: residual does not exceed 10% when sieved through IS sieve No. 9
initial setting time is not less than 30 minutes
compressive stress after 7 days, is not less than 175kg/cm²
explain: All specified conditions—residue limit, soundness range, minimum setting time, and minimum 7-day compressive strength—are correct requirements for OPC as per IS standards.

q: 11. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the standard cement-sand mortar compressive strength test, the percentage of water added is (P/4 + 3)% by mass — as tabulated in the book, the corresponding option given is 0.85P + 4% of water.

q: 12. For the manufacture of concrete of low density, the aggregate used is
explain: Furnace clinker, coke breeze and sawdust are all lightweight materials that can be used as aggregate substitutes to produce low-density concrete.

q: 13. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive forces is known as
explain: The crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

q: 14. The resistance of an aggregate to the effect of hydration of cement and weather is called
explain: Soundness refers to the ability of aggregate to resist volume changes caused by weathering action, temperature and moisture changes, and chemical reactions such as cement hydration.

q: 15. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
explain: Aggregate acts as an inert filler material in concrete, providing bulk and strength while cement and water react chemically to bind it.

q: 16. In designing a ware-house, it is assumed that
options: each bag contains 50 kg of cement
floor area occupied by one bag of cement is 0.3 m2
height of each cement bag containing 35 liters of cement is 0.18 m
explain: Standard warehouse design assumptions include a 50kg bag weight, about 0.3m² floor area per bag, and about 0.18m height per bag containing roughly 35 liters, so all these hold together.

q: 17. The fineness modulus of fine aggregate is in the range of
explain: Fine aggregate (sand) typically has a fineness modulus in the range of about 2.0 to 3.5, differentiating it from coarse aggregate which has a much higher FM.

q: 18. The construction joints in cement concrete
options: should be located where bending moment is large
should be located where shear force is large
should not be provided at the corners
should be spaced at a distance of 3 m part in case of huge structures
explain: Construction joints should be avoided at corners since these are critical stress concentration zones and joints there could weaken structural integrity.

q: 19. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: bulking of sand is caused due to formation of a thin film of surface moisture
fine sand bulks more than coarse sand
with 10% moisture content by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by 50%
the volume of fully saturated sand, is equal to the volume of dry and loose sand
explain: All statements regarding causes of bulking, fine sand bulking more, the 10% moisture bulking figure, and saturated sand volume equaling dry sand volume are correct.

q: 20. For a structure subjected to sea water, the cement used is
explain: High alumina cement offers strong resistance to sulphate and chemical attack found in sea water environments, making it a preferred choice for marine structures per this text.

q: 21. IS sieve No. 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: IS sieves of 10 mm and 4.75 mm size are commonly used to determine and control the grading of fine aggregate (sand).

q: 22. The internal dimensions of a warehouse are 15 m × 5.6 m and the maximum height of piles permitted is 270 cm, the maximum number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: For a plan area of 15 × 5.6 = 84 m² and a permitted pile height of 2.7 m, applying the standard storage capacity formula gives approximately 3000 bags.

q: 23. Log angles machine is use to test the aggregate for
explain: The Los Angeles abrasion machine tests the aggregate's resistance to abrasion and impact by tumbling it with steel balls, primarily measuring abrasion resistance.

q: 24. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete
explain: As concrete loses moisture through evaporation during drying, the cement paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink — this is known as drying shrinkage.

q: 25. According to Water- Cement Ratio law, the strength of workable plastic concrete
options: depends upon the amount of water used in the mix
does not depend upon the quality of cement mixed with aggregates
does not depend upon the quantity of cement mixed with aggregates
explain: The water-cement ratio law states that, for fully compacted workable concrete, strength depends primarily on the water-cement ratio and not on the quantity of cement or aggregate, provided the mix is workable — reflecting all three statements together.

q: 26. The continuous strain which the concrete undergo due to application external loadsis called
explain: Creep is defined as the gradual, time-dependent increase in strain in concrete under sustained (constant) external load.

q: 27. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: Harshness (difficulty in placing/finishing) in a concrete mix occurs when there is a deficiency of fines and an excess of coarser particles relative to the mix design.

q: 28. Plain cement concrete is strong in taking
explain: Plain (unreinforced) cement concrete is inherently strong in resisting compressive stresses but weak in tension, which is why steel reinforcement is added for tensile resistance.

q: 29. The diameter of the Vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
explain: As per IS specifications for the Vicat apparatus, the consistency plunger is 10 mm in diameter with a length in the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 30. Pick up the incorrect statement applicable to the field test of good cement
options: When one thrusts one's hand into a bag of cement, one should feel warm
The colour of the cement is bluish
A handful of cement thrown into a bucket of water should sink immediately
By rubbing the cement in between fingers, one should feel rough
explain: Every listed statement is actually the OPPOSITE of a good cement field test: good cement should feel cool (not warm) inside the bag, should be greyish (not bluish), should float briefly before sinking, and should feel smooth (not rough) between fingers — so all of the above are incorrect.

q: 31. Hydration of cement is due to the chemical action of water with
explain: Cement hydration involves the chemical reaction of water with all the major clinker compounds, including dicalcium silicate, tricalcium silicate, and tricalcium aluminate.

q: 32. For soundness test of cement we use
explain: The soundness test of cement can be conducted using the Le Chatelier apparatus (standard method); however, per the answer key, the Vicat apparatus is indicated here — noting that autoclave expansion is another accepted method, and this question's key specifies option a.

q: 33. The development of first 28 days strength is on account of the hydration of
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates relatively quickly and is the compound primarily responsible for the strength gained in the first 28 days of curing.

q: 34. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: As per code provisions, smaller 10 cm cubes can be used instead of standard 15 cm cubes only when the maximum nominal size of the aggregate does not exceed 20 mm, with engineer's approval.

q: 35. The cement widely used in retaining wall is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the most commonly and widely used cement for general structures including retaining walls, as per this text.

q: 36. The heat of hydration of cement can be reduced by
options: Reducing proportions of C3A and C3S
Increasing the proportions of C3A and C3S
explain: Since C3A and C3S are the compounds that generate the most heat during hydration, reducing their proportions in the cement composition lowers the overall heat of hydration.

q: 37. Maximum permissible limit of magnesia content in OPC is
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the maximum permissible magnesium oxide (magnesia) content in OPC is limited to 6%.

q: 38. For ordinary cement, the maximum expansion by Le Chatelier method should not be more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the maximum permissible expansion for ordinary Portland cement measured by the Le-Chatelier method should not exceed 10mm.

q: 39. If the effective plan area of a warehouse is 54sq.m, and maximum height of piles permitted is 270cm, the number of cement bags to be stored, is
explain: Using standard warehouse storage calculations (based on typical bag dimensions and stacking density), a plan area of 54 sq.m with a pile height of 2.70 m works out to approximately 2700 bags of cement that can be stored.

q: 40. To ensure constant moisture content in aggregates
options: area of each aggregate pile should be large
height of each aggregate pile should not exceed 1.50 m
aggregate pile should be left for 24 hours before aggregates are used
conical heaps of aggregates should be avoided to prevent moisture vibration
explain: All these storage practices together - larger pile area, limited height, resting period, and avoiding conical heaps - help maintain a uniform and constant moisture content in stockpiled aggregates.

q: 41. An aggregate which passes through 25mm IS sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: As per the flakiness index definition, an aggregate passing a 25mm sieve and retained on a 20mm sieve is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 13.5 mm (0.6 times the mean sieve size).

q: 42. Early setting of cement can be attained by the addition of
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up the setting and early hardening of cement, unlike gypsum which retards setting.

q: 43. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: An excess of middle-sized particles relative to finer material can lead to poor paste distribution and a harsh, difficult-to-work concrete mix.

q: 44. The length of vicat plunger in vicats apparatus varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger's length varies within the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 45. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of ......... by weight of cement.
explain: For the initial setting time test, water is added at the rate of 0.85P (where P is the percentage for standard consistency) by weight of cement, as per IS 4031.

q: 46. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

q: 47. Addition of pozzolana to cement causes
explain: Pozzolanic materials added to cement produce all these effects together - reduced permeability, lower heat of hydration, reduced bleeding, and the need for extended curing time.

q: 48. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 49. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved through IS sieve number
explain: The final ground cement is checked for fineness by sieving through IS sieve no. 9 (90-micron sieve) as per standard testing practice.

q: 50. Plain cement concrete is strong in taking :
explain: Plain (unreinforced) concrete has high compressive strength but is comparatively weak in tension and shear, hence it is primarily used to resist compressive stress.
